text:
claire: Heads up — onboarding sample on Vercel Edge failed with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED after the recent packaging tweak. Minimal repro below. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

devon: yup, just triaged a support ticket that sounds identical. Can you paste the import and package.json snippet?

claire: import used in edge worker: 
```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const cli = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await cli.generate('hello');
```
error: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './esm/index.mjs' is not defined by "exports"`
package.json (relevant): 
```json
{"name":"redwood-inference","version":"3.0.0","main":"cjs/index.cjs","exports":{"./esm/index.mjs":"cjs/index.cjs"},"types":"cjs/index.d.ts"}
```

rui: root cause: the exports map only points at the CJS file under the esm subpath. Edge platforms and bundlers expect an ESM import condition (and some will try to resolve ./esm/index.mjs). Because exports doesn't expose the package root (." ) or an import condition, the resolver throws. Also TypeScript/TS server can stop resolving types if exports is present but doesn't include types subpaths.

devon: exact. Node resolution and bundler/edge resolution diverge a lot here. Two practical fixes: (A) expose both import/require on the root export, or (B) publish a thin ESM entry that re-exports the CJS implementation. Example exports shape that worked in my local repro: 
```json
{"exports":{".":{"import":"esm/index.mjs","require":"cjs/index.cjs","types":"cjs/index.d.ts"},"./package.json":"./package.json"},"types":"cjs/index.d.ts"}
```
This ensures: - ESM consumers get the mjs file - CJS consumers get cjs - TS can find typings via the types subpath and top-level "types" fallback

sam: +1 on that mapping. Also, CI should catch this: add a quick smoke job that installs the SDK and runs our sample app in a Vercel Edge emulator and Cloudflare Pages preview for packaging-related PRs. We missed it because the packaging tweak was only unit-tested in Node CJS.

claire: customers report editor intellisense missing even after adding top-level "types". Any nuance there?

rui: TS behavior is quirky: when "exports" exists, Typescript prefers looking up types via export subpaths. If you only have top-level "types" but not a types export on the subpath consumers end up resolving, tssserver can still fail. Best practice we follow: keep top-level "types" and include a "types" field alongside import/require in the root export, and explicitly expose package.json if bundlers read it.

devon: short-term customer workarounds to share in support: 
- pin to previous patch that didn't change exports 
- import the ESM file path directly (e.g., `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/esm/index.mjs'`) 
Not great but workable while we publish a patch.

sam: agree we should ship a patch that reverts the export-only-CJS change, then follow up with a proper dual-export publish that includes types. Action plan: 
- devon: revert the packaging change + cut a patch release (P0)
- rui: add export mapping that includes import/require/types + ./package.json entry (P0)
- sam: add edge smoke matrix to CI for packaging PRs (P1)
- docs: short note in the SDK packaging doc about export maps, TS, and edge quirks (P2)

bot-deploy: CI pipeline started for revert branch (#3180) — smoke tests queued. :gear:

claire: thanks all. I'll attach the failing customer repro and point support to the workaround until the patch lands. Please ping me in the PR for verification on Vercel/Cloudflare previews. :thumbsup:
